plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding below my value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above risks winning at a loss. With a private value of $39, the optimal action is to bid exactly $39.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do—you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, so bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit. There's no incentive to shade the bid up or down, since overbidding risks paying more than the item's worth, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $27, I'll bid exactly that amount.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher than value risks overpaying if you win; bidding lower risks losing profitable deals. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $13, so I will bid exactly that amount.
